Update 12: Horses and Offline Application

8/2/2026 | Scott Petrovic

Horse Rig and base animations

This isn't just a bigger fox rig! The new horse rig is an entirely new creation with a set of 13 animations. Where the fox would have a more stealthy set of movements, the horse is more majestic by carrying itself up with its long neck and unique walking gaits. These animations will hopefully expand and improve as time goes on.

Work Offline

The Mesh2Motion app can now be used offline. This allows users to continue working on their projects without an internet connection. All the features in the online version work the same as in the offline version. This should have working versions on all the desktop operating systems like Windows, Mac, and Linux. This is the first release of this, so there might be bugs I didn't catch while testing.

Check out the downloads on Github: Offline Desktop App

Added 40 human animations

Because people can never have enough human animations. I have been getting random requests for the past couple of months and finally added some common ones. This brings the total count to over 160 animations for the human rig. Some of the animations are the following:

  • Strafing
  • Gliding
  • Ladder movement
  • More death animations
  • Bow and Arrow
  • Dodging
  • More zombie related animations

Improved bone visualization

The green "stick" skeletons were okay, but there were certain things that were difficult to communicate. These were the current issues:

  1. The orientation, or "bone roll", was impossible to see before. This is the rotation around the bone's local axis.
  2. With some of the rigs, the bones start overlapping each other and it is hard to tell them apart. This can make the bone placement more difficult.

With the new skeleton, it is easier to debug and see how the bones are rotating. There is a system to the colorization as well. Different bone types are categorized and colored differently. For example, spine-related bones are always green. This allows the "skinning" algorithm to do a better job by behaving differently depending on the bone type. This bone classification is pretty new. This is something I plan on developing more in the future.

Update 10: Spiders and Snakes

4/4/2026 | Scott Petrovic

Spider and Snake rig

The spider comes with 9 animations including the basics like idle, walk, attack, and death. The snake comes with 7 animations covering similar ground. Part of adding these was to expand the variety of rigs to see how well this tool can support different types of creatures.

Skeleton Editing Improvements

Easier to drag bone joints to the right position. The position will snap to the middle of the mesh. The other transform options also exist as a toggle if you want to still use that.

  • When moving bones with mirror mode, hide one side of bone joints to make positioning easier to see bones.
  • Add option to move bones independently so they don't affect the child bone positions.
  • Add an option for moving bones to volume center for easier placement

Update 9: Import Custom Animations

3/4/2026 | Scott Petrovic

Import custom animations

One issue that I had was trying to tell animators how to test their Blender animations in the Mesh2Motion app. There was no easy way without pulling down the source code and manually loading in their animation file. Now the workflow is much easier. Much faster and easier verification before they might submit their animations to be included.

This could also have a secondary benefit to allow people to make animation packs they could provide for free, or sell on sites like Gumroad. People could spend a bit of money and download a GLB file with animations. Those custom animations could then be imported into Mesh2Motion and used with the auto-rigging and default animations.

Other release notes

  • Added a number of Quaternius animations from his latest pack for the human rig.
  • Handle meshes with multiple materials on import. Previously there were errors when a mesh had multiple materials causing silent errors.
  • Retargeting: Fix animation data slowly getting messed up during retargeting process and export.
  • Retargeting: Make sure at least one bone mapping is done before allowing retargeting.
  • Retargeting: Shorten name for retargeting naming to "RT" to simplify names.
  • Move the toggle bone display to the player since import button expanded the tools area too much.
  • Updated human rig bones and animations to reflect new simplified bone naming.
  • Add contributor page to Github repository for better visibility.
  • Improve tooltip visuals and instructions for download button
  • Minor styling for back buttons in process to help visual flow.
  • Upgrade three.js code library to 182
  • Clean up dragon bones in skeleton file to only include "deform" bones

  • Roar
  • Swim

  • Tail Attack
  • Walk
  • Walk Root motion

Upload Your Rigged Mesh (Experimental)

Upload an already rigged mesh to use the Mesh2Motion animations. This is a large feature that is still a work in progress. I have been working on it for the past two months. I want to push out the current state to see if people even use this before developing it more. There are two main use cases I could find for this:

  1. You have a custom model that the Mesh2Motion web rigger cannot handle well. You want the animations, but you are a 3d person who wants control over the weight painting in your 3d tool. For this, people can use the Blender rig linked and do all the custom weight painting.
  2. People have rigged meshes that use other bone structures or naming. This could be from other tools that do rig generation and have the vertices assigned to the bones already.

The second use case with alternate bone names is where the feature gets complex. There are two main areas to think about when working with alternative bone structures. There is bone mapping, and there is bone roll. Bone mapping can be done manually, by assigning one named bone to another. Common mappings can use a template to go from one bone format to another.

The "bone roll" correction is often needed in addition to the bone map process. Even if two bones look the same, one could be rotated differently along the axis that pierces through the ends. If this orientation is different, all the rotation data is going to be wrong. A new contributor (Sketchpunklabs) provided an algorithm/example to accomplish this. This was extremely helpful.
